messages:
olivia: Heads-up — usw1 dedicated pool-14 showing a 99p token-latency jump since ~11:20 UTC. Impacting some dedicated tenants. Telemetry points to GPU PCIe stalls + NIC transmit bursts, anyone oncall?

mike: Saw it, triaging now. Pushed the perf dashboard: https://grafana/redwood/d/allocs/usw1-pool14 :eyes:

priya: Which tenant is noisy? Can we soft-isolate before draining hosts?

olivia: Tenant mlprep-42. Affected host node-gpu-az14-03. Quick dmesg tail:```
[ 5402.123456] pcieport 0000:3f:01.0: AER: Corrected error: 00000000
[ 5402.123470] pcieport 0000:3f:01.0: AER: Device recovery failed
[ 5403.001200] mlx5_core 0000:5e:00.0: TX queue burst detected
```

sam: `kubectl get pods -o wide | grep node-gpu-az14-03` shows 6 pods, one heavy batch-prep job (mlprep-42-batch). Suggest evicting that pod to warm pool.

mike: Evict attempt failed due to strict nodeAffinity on that pod (customer-managed). Workaround: temp carve a dedicated slice and re-route mlprep-42. Cost estimate ~\$1.8k/day for 4xA100 (ballpark). Approving temporary carve if router change can't avoid it.

priya: Let's try routing change first. Adding a `noisy_neighbor=true` tag and soft-isolate rule in router: `if noisy_neighbor then route->dedicated_preemptable=true` — I'll push a 1% canary patch.

olivia: Canary pushed to us-west-1 router (1%): observed 99p latency for mlprep-42 dropped from 4.9s -> 1.1s. Looks promising. :thumbsup:

sam: Good. Still seeing NIC TX bursts on node-gpu-az14-03 though — hardware/driver might need attention. Should we open a HW ticket?

mike: Open HW ticket and schedule host drain. I'll run `fleetctl drain node-gpu-az14-03 --reason 'pcie_aer'` in a 10m window once canary verified.

priya: Notified product-sre and customer-success to give the customer a heads-up. Also annotating tenant ledger: `noisy-eject:oncall-mitigation`.

olivia: If drain forces preemptible fallbacks and causes regressions, fallback policy should route requests to the quantized model variant (lower mem) to avoid spinning up extra slices — cheaper and faster.

sam: Runbook follow-up: add AER/dmesg check to noisefence sentinel and an automatic routing toggle. I'll open PR with the check and tests.

mike: :white_check_mark: Action items: mike -> drain + HW ticket, priya -> router patch & CS note, sam -> runbook PR, olivia -> follow-up latency & cost calc. Recheck in 30m.

olivia: Note for follow-up: consider permanent dedicated carveouts for long-running prep jobs (they repeatedly hit noisefence). tagging finance for cost model.

finance-bot: Created ticket FIN-9123 to analyze recurring "dedicated-slice" costs for long-running batch jobs. ETA 3d.
